100 % à distance · Organisation libre · Commission sur les ventes issues de vos recommandations

Vous aimez créer des contacts, repérer des opportunités et mettre les bonnes personnes en relation ?

Avec PropertyOS, vous identifiez des propriétaires, bailleurs ou petites agences intéressés par une gestion immobilière plus simple. Vous organisez le rendez-vous : le fondateur assure la démonstration et le closing.

🏡 PropertyOS, c’est quoi ?

PropertyOS est une plateforme SaaS qui centralise les biens immobiliers, les locataires, les finances, les documents et les tâches dans un même espace.

Notre ambition : permettre aux propriétaires et gestionnaires de gagner du temps et de garder une vision claire de leur activité immobilière.

La plateforme est accessible directement en ligne. Nous développons également un réseau de partenaires indépendants pour la faire découvrir à de nouveaux clients grâce à une approche plus personnelle.

🎯 Votre mission : créer des opportunités qualifiées

Votre rôle consiste à :

  • Identifier des propriétaires bailleurs, investisseurs et petites agences susceptibles d’être intéressés.

  • Entrer en contact avec eux et comprendre leur organisation actuelle.

  • Présenter simplement PropertyOS et son intérêt.

  • Vérifier leur intérêt pour une démonstration et pour le budget proposé.

  • Organiser un rendez-vous avec le fondateur.

  • Enregistrer les informations utiles dans PropertyOS Advisor pour préparer l’échange.

Vous vous concentrez sur la prospection et la mise en relation. Le fondateur prend ensuite le relais pour la démonstration détaillée, les questions commerciales, la négociation et la conclusion de l’abonnement.

Vous ne négociez pas les conditions et ne signez pas de contrat au nom de PropertyOS.

⚡ PropertyOS Advisor : votre application partenaire

Vous disposez de PropertyOS Advisor, notre application dédiée aux apporteurs d’affaires.

Pensée pour fluidifier votre activité, elle vous permet de centraliser les informations de vos prospects, suivre vos mises en relation et transmettre le contexte nécessaire à la préparation des rendez-vous.

L’objectif : une prospection organisée et un passage de relais simple, pour donner à chaque opportunité les meilleures chances d’aboutir.

💸 Une rémunération liée aux clients apportés

L’offre mise en avant dans ce partenariat est l’abonnement annuel PropertyOS à 990 €.

Vous percevez une commission pour chaque nouveau client qui souscrit et règle cet abonnement à la suite de votre mise en relation, selon les conditions prévues au contrat.

  • Rémunération à la commission uniquement.

  • Aucun salaire fixe ni revenu garanti.

  • Le montant de la commission et le calendrier de versement sont communiqués avant tout engagement.

  • Les règles d’attribution des prospects, de traitement des doublons et d’annulation sont précisées au contrat.

  • Un rendez-vous seul ne déclenche pas de commission : celle-ci dépend de la souscription et de l’encaissement correspondants.

👋 À qui s’adresse cette opportunité ?

À des personnes autonomes, à l’aise dans les échanges et capables de créer un premier contact de qualité.

Vous pouvez avoir une expérience commerciale, un réseau dans l’immobilier ou simplement une vraie capacité à prospecter avec méthode.

Nous recherchons surtout :

  • De l’écoute, pour repérer un besoin réel.

  • De la clarté, pour expliquer la solution sans faire de promesses excessives.

  • De la régularité, pour développer votre activité.

  • De la rigueur, pour transmettre des informations fiables.

  • Un bon relationnel, pour représenter PropertyOS avec professionnalisme.

Une expérience en prospection, en immobilier ou dans le SaaS est un atout. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être un expert du logiciel ni un closer confirmé.

🌴 Notre culture : détendue, directe et orientée résultats

Chez PropertyOS, on apprécie les échanges simples, les idées utiles et les personnes qui prennent des initiatives.

Vous organisez librement votre activité : pas d’horaires imposés ni de volume hebdomadaire obligatoire. Cette collaboration peut compléter d’autres activités professionnelles.

Notre façon d’avancer : partager les retours du terrain, améliorer les approches et privilégier des mises en relation pertinentes.

Une ambiance chill, des engagements tenus et des opportunités concrètes.

🤝 Pour bien démarrer

La prise en main comprend :

  • Une présentation de PropertyOS et de ses principaux cas d’usage.

  • La découverte de PropertyOS Advisor.

  • Des repères pour identifier les profils de clients recherchés.

  • Des supports pour présenter la solution.

  • Une explication du processus de mise en relation et de rémunération.

Vous avez un interlocuteur direct pour transmettre vos questions et vos retours.

📋 Cadre de la collaboration

Nature : partenariat indépendant d’apport d’affaires, sans contrat de travail.
Lieu : à distance, depuis la France.
Organisation : libre, sans exclusivité.
Démarrage : à convenir ensemble.

Vous devez disposer d’une activité indépendante déclarée et d’un SIRET pour exercer depuis la France. La micro-entreprise est une possibilité.

Vous pouvez candidater avant d’avoir créé votre activité, mais les formalités nécessaires devront être réalisées pour démarrer la collaboration.

Un contrat écrit définit les missions, les commissions et les conditions du partenariat.

🚀 Intéressé ? Présentez-vous simplement.

Envoyez-nous quelques lignes sur :

  • Votre parcours et votre éventuelle expérience en prospection.

  • Les types de prospects que vous pourriez contacter.

  • Votre statut actuel et vos disponibilités pour démarrer.

Vous créez le contact. Nous prenons le relais pour transformer l’intérêt en abonnement.

Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at ScholarRock.com and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.

The Patient Advocacy & Corporate Communications Lead, EMEA will be responsible for developing and executing integrated patient advocacy and communications strategies that advance the company's mission, strengthen stakeholder trust, and support business objectives across the region, starting with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) and including  facioscapulohumeral dystrophy (FSHD) in line with clinical development milestones. 

This role will serve as the primary EMEA lead for patient advocacy engagement while also driving corporate and product communications, executive visibility, disease awareness initiatives, and internal communications. The successful candidate will engage the SMA community (and communities for future disease states) to establish and solidify trust and act as a connector to patient and advocate perspectives to drive Scholar Rock’s patient first values. They will act as a trusted strategic advisor to regional leadership and work cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Global patient advocacy and communications, Market Access, Clinical Development, Regulatory, and Commercial Teams, supported by global and regional agency partners.

Patient Advocacy Leadership
Develop and Execute Advocacy Strategy

Sonar is driving the future of agent-centric software development. As the leader in AI code verification and governance, we solve a critical problem: ensuring that software generated by AI-assisted developers or autonomous agents is reliable, secure, and maintainable.

About Welo Global 

Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com  


The Role 

We are seeking an experienced English into German (Switzerland) Review Lead to serve as the language quality owner and primary client-facing linguistic expert for a leading global technology client. 

You will own the locale’s interpretation of the client’s quality standards and make sure that the Post-Editing Lead, Post Editors, and Reviewers all work to the same shared understanding of “good”. You will be the main point of contact for the client’s Language Manager on quality discussions, arbitration, and escalations, and you will drive consistency, quality governance, and continuous improvement across UI, marketing, product, informational, legal, and support content. 

Project Details 

- Location: Remote (based in one of the approved countries below)
- Expected volume: Approximately 24 hours per month
- Employment type: Freelance / Independent Contract
- Task type: Language Lead Support
- Content types: UI, Marketing, Informational, Legal, Product, Support
- Language pair: English into German from Switzerland

What You Will Do 

-Analyse requirements: Review every style guide and glossary update, assess which quality categories and content types it affects, and record the changes. Track what the client’s Language Manager actually corrects and says in calibration and quality calls, not only what is written down.
-Relay expectations: Run regular alignment roundtables with the language community and publish a structured monthly quality digest covering performance, priority improvement areas, style guide updates, and notable errors and arbitration outcomes.
-Manage review quality actively: Coach Reviewers one-to-one using specific examples, run shadowing sessions, and deliver training built from real alignment data.
-Improve the standard: Turn recurring justification patterns into well-reasoned style guide proposals, and share cross-locale patterns with the Welocalize Quality Manager.
-Maintain alignment with the client: Treat Language Manager decisions as the standard, raise concerns with evidence at the right forum, and aim for fewer surprises over time.

What You Will Own

-The locale’s review service score, including RQE audit and alignment performance
-The community’s shared understanding of quality 
-The integrity of the arbitration record, ensuring that every arbitration sent to the client is valid and well-evidenced
-The working relationship with the client’s Language Manager, including clarifications, escalations, and expectation tracking

Requirements

- Experience: 3 to 5+ years in Localization Quality Assurance (LQA), Senior Language Lead, or Quality Governance roles
- Client and stakeholder management: Direct experience as the primary point of contact for client Language Managers, managing formal arbitration or escalation processes, and facilitating conflict resolution
- Quality audit frameworks: Deep, practical experience with localization evaluation frameworks, including RQE, LQE, error rubrics, and severity mapping
- Style guide and expectation analysis: Ability to analyse style guide changes, identify implicit client expectations, and map tolerance by content type (for example, Marketing vs. Legal vs. UI)
- Meeting facilitation: Hands-on experience with one-to-one coaching, shadowing sessions, alignment roundtables, and structured monthly quality reporting
- Analytical approach: Skill in tracking error concentrations, severity drift, and alignment scores, and in converting justification patterns into style guide improvements
- Language: Native-level German (Switzerland) and professional-level English
- Preferred: Prior experience supporting major technology localization programs and working with calibration or alignment tools

Additional Key Information 

- Successful candidates will be provided with a dedicated device for project work.
- A background check is required as part of onboarding.
- Candidates must be physically located in one of the approved countries.

Approved countries: Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Egypt, El Salvador, Finland, France, Germany, Ghana, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Lithuania, Malaysia, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Nigeria, Norway, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States and Vietnam.

This role offers a long-term partnership with global teams on high-visibility products. You will benefit from steady project volume, comprehensive onboarding and ongoing upskilling, and access to established linguistic resources.

About Us

Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. We are a high-performance, high-collaboration team that thrives on solving complex problems, moving fast, and delivering impact.

Role Outcome

The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally handle complex technical support cases while also leading the operational systems, monitoring, and processes that ensure the network performs reliably at scale.

Success in this role means:

  • Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers.

  • When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis.

  • The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction.

  • A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow.

Immediate Areas of Focus

Own the customer experience of our Network

  • Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience

  • Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues.

  • Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions.

Deliver High-Quality Technical Support

  • Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer.

  • Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases.

  • Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents.

  • Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team.

Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function

  • Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale.

  • Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact.

  • Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as:

    • Network uptime and availability

    • Incident response and resolution times

    • Support response and resolution times

    • Alert quality and monitoring coverage

    • Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models.

  • Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.

Surface Operational and Customer Insights

  • Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data.

  • Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering.

  • Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized.

  • Create lightweight reporting that gives leadership visibility into network reliability, operational trends, and customer friction.

Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience

  • Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact.

  • Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise.

  • Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement.

Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function

  • Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team.

  • Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication.

  • Establish clear expectations for technical depth, ownership, and responsiveness.

  • Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows.

Qualifications

  • Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

  • Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems.

  • Strong technical background in GPS/GNSS, precise localization, geospatial infrastructure, or closely related domains (robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, positioning technologies).

  • Experience operating or supporting distributed infrastructure or network-based systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to build or significantly improve monitoring, alerting, and operational processes.

  • Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems and working directly with customers.

  • Experience conducting incident response and root cause analysis.

  • Ability to define metrics, processes, and documentation without over-engineering.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and Go-To-Market teams in a fast-moving environment.

  • Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Our Cultural Foundation

At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position.

This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact. It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them.

That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today, not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows.

We think about our culture in two dimensions:

How We Show Up Every Day

These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate:

  • Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting.

  • High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us.

  • Divine Discontent — We’re never satisfied with the status quo and are self-motivated to improve ourselves, our work, and our company. We actively seek feedback in real-time to shorten improvement cycles.

  • No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together.

  • Self Accountability — Taking ownership is the straightest line to learning, self-improvement, and correcting our course of action. And blaming others around us is a fast path to destroying trust.

Operating Principles

These are the systems and norms that amplify speed and efficiency at the company level:

  • Edge Innovation — We bias toward action over approval. Experiment, decide, and move — failure is just a step toward faster learning.

  • No Hierarchies — We practice self-prioritization and go direct to the source. Flattening layers reduces drag and maximizes autonomy.

  • Customer Experience First — We optimize for the end-to-end customer outcome, not functional or departmental efficiency. This focus cuts waste, aligns priorities, and ensures we spend effort where it matters most.

If this role sounds like a fit, we’d love to hear from you. Apply below and join us in shaping the future of precise location.

About Rivia

Rivia is a technology company building a data engine that powers the future of clinical trial intelligence. Rivia was founded on the belief that new drugs can be brought to market more successfully with a fraction of today's capital.

Biotechs are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is constantly constrained by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia unifies clinical trial data at scale through a core engine built as a reusable intelligence layer, comprising hundreds of configurations and trial-specific logic, independent of source structure. This vertical stack of data engine, workflows, and agents creates a distinct advantage in how trials are operated.

Over the past two years, European and US based biotechs running global clinical trials on Rivia have demonstrated measurable impact, from earlier understanding of therapeutic potential to significantly more efficient trial execution. In March 2026, Rivia raised its $15M Series A led by Earlybird Venture Capital.

Rivia’s ambition is to become the standard infrastructure for modern drug development, transforming how trials are executed end-to-end.

The Role

As our Senior Talent & People Partner, you will be the first hire in Rivia’s People team, working directly alongside the Head of People to build and scale the function from the ground up. You’ll own Talent Acquisition end to end while growing into the broader world of People: employee experience, development, performance, culture, organizational design, and operations.

This is an opportunity for a strong recruiter ready to make the leap into a broader People role. You won't inherit a fully established HR playbook. Together, we'll create processes, solve unfamiliar problems, test ideas, and build the foundations that help Rivia scale. You'll learn directly from the Head of People through hands-on ownership, close collaboration, and exposure to both strategic decisions and operational challenges.

Think of yourself as the Head of People's partner in crime: an independent thinker, trusted collaborator, and hands-on builder who brings ideas, challenges assumptions, moves quickly, and follows through. We want someone who understands the business behind the People work and wants to become a true advisor to leaders, not just a process executor.

What Excites You

  • You love recruiting, but want to grow beyond Talent Acquisition and learn the full People spectrum.

  • Being the first People team hire and building from scratch sounds more exciting than maintaining an established playbook.

  • Working closely with the Head of People, challenging ideas, and learning through real ownership.

  • Finding exceptional talent and building trusted partnerships with hiring managers.

  • Solving ambiguous business and people problems with speed, curiosity, and pragmatism.

  • Creating better employee experiences, growth opportunities, and ways of working.

  • Taking initiative, juggling priorities, and seeing the impact of your work directly.

Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition

  • Own end-to-end hiring across teams, including role definition, Talent Mapping, sourcing, interviews, candidate management, offers, and closing.

  • Be a true advisor to hiring managers on hiring strategy, market realities, candidate quality, and trade-offs.

  • Build proactive pipelines and deliver a thoughtful, responsive candidate experience.

  • Improve hiring processes, ATS workflows, reporting, and recruitment analytics.

Employee Experience & Development

  • Co-build onboarding, employee experience, engagement, culture, and development initiatives with the Head of People.

  • Help implement performance reviews, feedback practices, career development, and manager enablement.

  • Listen to employee and manager needs, identify friction, and turn insights into practical improvements.

People Operations & Business Partnership

  • Help build scalable People processes, policies, systems, and employee lifecycle workflows from the ground up.

  • Support managers with pragmatic, business-aware advice and thoughtful people decisions.

  • Contribute to projects across organizational design, compensation, HR operations, and People analytics as your scope grows.

  • Spot problems early, propose solutions, and own implementation rather than waiting for instructions.

What Excites Us

  • Professional proficiency in German.

  • Strong end-to-end Talent Acquisition experience and evidence of independently delivering high-quality hires.

  • Ambition to pivot into a broader People role; previous generalist experience is not required.

  • A builder and problem-solver who acts quickly, thinks critically, and takes ownership through execution.

  • Business acumen and confidence to challenge, influence, and advise hiring managers and leaders.

  • Comfort with ambiguity, high expectations, multiple priorities, and hands-on work.

  • Excellent communication, judgment, organization, and stakeholder management.

  • Curiosity, humility, and willingness to learn new People disciplines.

Nice to Have

  • Knowledge of Swiss employment and labour law.

  • Exposure to employee development, performance management, or employee engagement.

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up and familiarity with ATS, HRIS, or People analytics.

Hiring Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks across four stages:

  1. Recruiter Interview: 30-minute introductory conversation with the People team.

  2. Deep dive: Conversation with the Head of People about recruitment, business partnership, and growth ambitions.

  3. Practical case 1: Step by Step on how to fill the Head of People role.

  4. On-site: Final stage in our Zürich office to explore mutual fit.

Our Values

At Rivia, we are committed to excellence, continuous learning, and the success of both our customers and our team.

  • In it to Win it: Approach challenges with determination, resilience, and drive.

  • Embrace change: See change as an opportunity to improve.

  • Why not?: Challenge assumptions and stay curious.

  • Find the gap: Proactively identify and solve problems.

  • Collective accountability: Own outcomes together and support one another.

  • Value add solutions: Deliver meaningful, impactful results.

Über Rivia

Rivia ist ein Technologieunternehmen, das eine Datenplattform entwickelt, die die Zukunft der klinischen Studienanalyse prägt. Rivia wurde aus der Überzeugung heraus gegründet, dass sich neue Medikamente mit einem Bruchteil des heutigen Kapitals erfolgreicher auf den Markt bringen lassen.

Biotech-Unternehmen sind die wichtigste Quelle therapeutischer Innovationen. Ihre klinische Entwicklung wird jedoch immer wieder durch fragmentierte Daten und veraltete Werkzeuge ausgebremst. Rivia führt klinische Studiendaten in großem Maßstab zusammen. Das Herzstück ist eine wiederverwendbare intelligente Datenplattform mit Hunderten von Konfigurationen und studienspezifischen Logiken, die unabhängig von der Struktur der Quelldaten funktioniert. Diese vertikal integrierte Kombination aus Datenplattform, Workflows und KI-Agenten schafft einen entscheidenden Vorteil bei der Durchführung klinischer Studien.

In den vergangenen zwei Jahren haben Biotech-Unternehmen aus Europa und den USA, die mit Rivia weltweit klinische Studien durchführen, messbare Ergebnisse erzielt: von einem früheren Verständnis des therapeutischen Potenzials bis hin zu deutlich effizienteren Studienabläufen. Im März 2026 nahm Rivia in einer Series-A-Finanzierungsrunde 15 Millionen US-Dollar auf, angeführt von Earlybird Venture Capital.

Rivia will zur Standardinfrastruktur für die moderne Arzneimittelentwicklung werden und die Durchführung klinischer Studien von Anfang bis Ende grundlegend verändern.

Die Rolle

Als Senior Talent & People Partner bist du die erste Verstärkung im People-Team von Rivia. Gemeinsam mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs baust du die Funktion von Grund auf auf und entwickelst sie weiter. Du verantwortest den gesamten Recruiting-Prozess und wächst zugleich in weitere People-Themen hinein: Mitarbeitererfahrung, Entwicklung, Performance, Unternehmenskultur, Organisationsgestaltung und Personalprozesse.

Die Position bietet erfahrenen Recruiter:innen die Möglichkeit, den nächsten Schritt in eine umfassendere People-Rolle zu machen. Ein fertiges HR-Handbuch, das du einfach übernimmst, gibt es nicht. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir Prozesse, lösen neue Herausforderungen, probieren Ideen aus und schaffen die Grundlagen für das Wachstum von Rivia. Durch praktische Verantwortung, enge Zusammenarbeit und Einblicke in strategische Entscheidungen wie auch operative Herausforderungen lernst du direkt von der Leitung des People-Bereichs.

Du bist die enge Sparringspartner:in der Leitung des People-Bereichs: Du denkst selbstständig, arbeitest vertrauensvoll zusammen und packst mit an. Du bringst Ideen ein, hinterfragst Annahmen, handelst schnell und setzt Vorhaben konsequent um. Gesucht ist jemand, der versteht, wie People-Arbeit zum Geschäftserfolg beiträgt, und Führungskräfte wirklich beraten möchte – statt lediglich Prozesse abzuarbeiten.

Was dich begeistert

  • Du liebst Recruiting, möchtest dich aber über Talent Acquisition hinaus weiterentwickeln und das gesamte People-Spektrum kennenlernen.

  • Die erste Person im People-Team zu sein und alles von Grund auf mit aufzubauen, reizt dich mehr, als ein bestehendes Handbuch zu pflegen.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs zusammen, hinterfragst Ideen und lernst durch echte Verantwortung.

  • Du findest außergewöhnliche Talente und baust vertrauensvolle Partnerschaften mit den einstellenden Führungskräften auf.

  • Du löst komplexe Geschäfts- und People-Fragen schnell, neugierig und pragmatisch.

  • Du möchtest die Mitarbeitererfahrung, Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten und Zusammenarbeit verbessern.

  • Du ergreifst die Initiative, behältst verschiedene Prioritäten im Blick und siehst direkt, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.

Deine Aufgaben

Talent Acquisition

  • Du verantwortest den gesamten Einstellungsprozess über alle Teams hinweg – von der Definition der Rolle über Talent Mapping, Active Sourcing, Interviews und die Betreuung der Kandidat:innen bis hin zu Angeboten und Vertragsabschlüssen.

  • Du berätst einstellende Führungskräfte fundiert zu Recruiting-Strategie, Marktbedingungen, Qualität der Kandidat:innen und möglichen Kompromissen.

  • Du baust proaktiv Talent-Pipelines auf und sorgst für eine wertschätzende, verlässliche Candidate Experience.

  • Du verbesserst Recruiting-Prozesse, ATS-Workflows, Reporting und Recruiting-Analysen.

Mitarbeitererfahrung und Entwicklung

  • Gemeinsam mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs entwickelst du Onboarding, Mitarbeitererfahrung, Engagement, Unternehmenskultur und Entwicklungsinitiativen weiter.

  • Du unterstützt die Einführung von Performance Reviews, Feedback-Praktiken, Karriereentwicklung und Angeboten für Führungskräfte.

  • Du hörst den Anliegen von Mitarbeitenden und Führungskräften zu, erkennst Reibungspunkte und setzt Erkenntnisse in konkrete Verbesserungen um.

People Operations und Business-Partnerschaft

  • Du hilfst dabei, skalierbare People-Prozesse, Richtlinien, Systeme und Abläufe entlang des gesamten Beschäftigungsverhältnisses von Grund auf aufzubauen.

  • Du unterstützt Führungskräfte mit pragmatischer, geschäftsorientierter Beratung und durchdachten Personalentscheidungen.

  • Mit wachsendem Verantwortungsbereich arbeitest du an Projekten zu Organisationsgestaltung, Vergütung, HR Operations und People Analytics mit.

  • Du erkennst Probleme früh, schlägst Lösungen vor und kümmerst dich um deren Umsetzung, statt auf Anweisungen zu warten.

Was du mitbringst

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse.

  • Umfassende Erfahrung im Recruiting über den gesamten Einstellungsprozess hinweg sowie nachweisbare Erfolge bei der eigenständigen Besetzung anspruchsvoller Positionen.

  • Den Wunsch, dich in eine umfassendere People-Rolle weiterzuentwickeln; Erfahrung als HR-Generalist:in ist nicht erforderlich.

  • Du baust gern Neues auf, löst Probleme, handelst schnell, denkst kritisch und übernimmst Verantwortung bis zur Umsetzung.

  • Geschäftssinn und die Sicherheit, einstellende Führungskräfte und andere Verantwortliche zu hinterfragen, zu überzeugen und zu beraten.

  • Du fühlst dich wohl mit offenen Fragestellungen, hohen Erwartungen, mehreren parallelen Prioritäten und praktischer Arbeit.

  • Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit, gutes Urteilsvermögen, Organisationstalent und Erfahrung im Stakeholder-Management.

  • Neugier, Bescheidenheit und die Bereitschaft, neue People-Fachgebiete zu erschließen.

Von Vorteil

  • Kenntnisse des Schweizer Arbeitsrechts.

  • Einblicke in Mitarbeiterentwicklung, Performance Management oder Mitarbeiterengagement.

  • Erfahrung in einem Startup oder Scale-up sowie Vertrautheit mit ATS-, HRIS- oder People-Analytics-Systemen.

Bewerbungsprozess

Unser Bewerbungsprozess dauert in der Regel zwei bis vier Wochen und umfasst vier Schritte:

  1. Kennenlernen: 30-minütiges erstes Gespräch mit dem People-Team.

  2. Vertiefendes Gespräch: Austausch mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs über Recruiting, Business-Partnerschaft und deine Entwicklungsziele.

  3. Praxisaufgabe: Gemeinsame Bearbeitung einer realistischen Recruiting- und People-Herausforderung.

  4. Kennenlernen des Teams: Gespräche vor Ort in Zürich, um herauszufinden, ob wir gut zueinander passen.

Unsere Werte

Bei Rivia setzen wir auf Spitzenleistung, kontinuierliches Lernen und den Erfolg unserer Kund:innen und unseres Teams.

  • Mit vollem Einsatz gewinnen: Herausforderungen mit Entschlossenheit, Ausdauer und Tatkraft angehen.

  • Veränderung annehmen: Wandel als Chance zur Verbesserung sehen.

  • Warum eigentlich nicht?: Annahmen hinterfragen und neugierig bleiben.

  • Lücken erkennen: Probleme frühzeitig identifizieren und lösen.

  • Gemeinsam Verantwortung übernehmen: Zusammen für Ergebnisse einstehen und einander unterstützen.

  • Lösungen mit Mehrwert schaffen: Sinnvolle Ergebnisse erzielen, die wirklich etwas bewirken.

data.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

 

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

 

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

  • Coaching: you have coached or mentored other engineers and help technical project managers grow.

  • Scope: you own our Oracle integrations end to end, set technical direction and take on the most complex customer cases.

Why BLP

  • Real impact: your integrations decide whether a customer goes live.

  • Breadth: Oracle, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and many other ERPs, plus EDI and e-invoicing standards.

  • Growth: fast-tracked growth, with promotions and a bonus scheme that includes company shares.

  • Team: regular team events.

Practical information

  • Location: our Zurich office, hybrid with 3+ office days per week, or remotely from anywhere in Europe.

  • If you work remotely, we pay for regular visits and stays in Zurich.

  • Employment: full-time, permanent.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation and control stack of the fusion energy reactors of the future.

Our technology enables effective and reliable operation, monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices — which will one day provide clean, practically limitless power to the grid. We have spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and have just completed our pre-seed fundraise.

We are looking for a Senior Control Systems Engineer to join our founding team in Lausanne and help build our core technology.

This job is for you if you are a passionate engineer with deep knowledge cutting across real-time / embedded systems, software and hardware, and excited about building the systems to monitor and control real-world fusion plasmas.

Tasks

  • Implement real-time control, analysis, data acquisition systems in the kHz to MHz range, as individual contributor and in a team.
  • Integrate solutions across a variety of company products and services as well as on our in-house test beds.
  • Provide technical leadership within a growing real-time control and software engineering team that you will help to build.
  • Translate customer needs into requirements and specifications.

Requirements

  • Experience taking hard-real-time acquisition and control loops from incomplete requirements through to commissioning on hardware, in domains such as automotive, robotics, embedded, electrical and/or scientific instrumentation.
  • ‘Full stack’: familiarity with all aspects of real-time technologies, from physical/DAQ, real-time software frameworks and middleware, real-time OS and integration.
  • Fluency in a mix of high-level and low-level languages such as C, C++, Rust, MATLAB/Simulink, Python. Obsession with code quality, testing and reliability.
  • Experience with distributed real-time systems, real-time networking and field buses and/or SCADA is an advantage.
  • Experience with embedded/μC/FPGA technologies and/or safety critical systems is an advantage.

Benefits

  • The unique opportunity to play a foundational role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up.
  • The opportunity to build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts.
  • Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life.
  • Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance.

If you are excited about joining our team, send your CV including information about a real-time system you have taken into operation. We're looking forward to hearing from you.

The role

H55 is looking for a versatile and hands on Head of Finance & Administration to lead its corporate functions and ensure the effective running of its Swiss site.

This broad leadership role combines a solid finance background with strong corporate governance and practical operational management. Working closely with the CEO and leadership team, you will connect people, priorities and resources, providing the structure and support needed to deliver the company’s business objectives.

You will develop a thorough understanding of H55’s corporate framework, including its shareholder arrangements, financing agreements and key contractual commitments, and translate these obligations into clear responsibilities, practical policies and timely action.

You will oversee finance, HR, IT, facilities and general administration, supported by internal specialists and external partners. As a central point of coordination for Swiss site matters, you will help teams resolve operational issues, improve ways of working and ensure corporate services meet the needs of the business.

Key responsibilities

Corporate governance and administration

  • Coordinate Board and shareholder matters with the CEO and legal counsel, including meeting preparation, resolutions, corporate records and follow through on decisions.

  • Maintain a clear overview of the company’s corporate structure, shareholder arrangements, financing agreements and material contractual commitments.

  • Track related obligations and deadlines, ensuring clear ownership and timely action across relevant functions.

  • Ensure governance requirements, delegated authorities and approval processes are understood and applied.

  • Manage relationships with external legal advisers, insurers and corporate service providers.

Policies, compliance and internal controls

  • Coordinate the development, implementation and review of company policies in line with business needs, investor commitments and applicable requirements.

  • Work with functional owners on anti corruption, cybersecurity and incident response, related party transactions, internal financial controls, global trade controls, personal data protection, and health and safety.

  • Translate policies into practical procedures, with clear responsibilities and guidance for employees and managers.

  • Coordinate communication and training, maintaining appropriate records.

  • Monitor implementation, address gaps with relevant owners and bring matters requiring attention to the leadership team.

Swiss site and corporate services

  • Coordinate Swiss site administration and corporate support activities, working closely with production, engineering and other teams.

  • Oversee facilities, workplace services and external providers, ensuring a safe and effective working environment.

  • Help resolve site issues and coordinate improvements that support daily operations.

  • Oversee IT services and infrastructure through internal resources and external partners.

  • Drive improvements in digital tools, systems and administrative processes.

  • Coordinate site procedures and business continuity arrangements with relevant specialists.

HR oversight and organisational support

  • Oversee the HR function, supporting the HR team in delivering effective people processes and reliable daily operations.

  • Work with the CEO and managers on workforce planning, organisational changes and recruitment priorities.

  • Ensure employment administration, payroll coordination and HR policies are managed consistently and appropriately.

  • Support clear internal communication and effective collaboration across teams.

Financial management and business support

  • Oversee budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning and financial reporting, supported by internal finance resources and external partners.

  • Ensure reliable accounting, statutory reporting, tax and audit processes.

  • Provide clear financial visibility to support business decisions and resource allocation.

  • Maintain appropriate financial controls, spending discipline and approval processes.

  • Monitor costs and commitments with budget owners and programme teams.

  • Support investor reporting, financing activities and due diligence when required.

Leadership and continuous improvement

  • Lead and support a small multidisciplinary team, coordinating external expertise where needed.

  • Set priorities, allocate resources and ensure actions are completed.

  • Build trusted working relationships with managers and colleagues across the organisation.

  • Simplify processes and adapt corporate services as the business evolves.

Your profile

  • Experience in a broad finance and administration, corporate services or business operations leadership role.

  • A solid finance background, with experience taking responsibility beyond the finance function.

  • Strong understanding of corporate governance and confidence working with corporate documents, contractual commitments and legal advisers.

  • Experience implementing policies and translating compliance requirements into practical ways of working.

  • Experience coordinating site operations or corporate support functions, ideally in a technology or industrial environment.

  • Familiarity with the Swiss business environment and relevant administrative and statutory requirements.

  • Ability to lead across different functions, drawing on the expertise of colleagues and external partners.

  • Sound judgement, discretion and the ability to build trust with people across the organisation.

  • A practical, collaborative approach, with strong organisational skills and a willingness to get involved in day to day matters.

  • Fluent English and French.

  • A relevant qualification in finance, business administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

You do not need to be a specialist in every function. You should be comfortable asking the right questions, bringing together the right expertise and taking responsibility for progress.

Why join H55?

At H55, you will work closely with the people developing electric aviation technology and help create the conditions for them to succeed. Your decisions will shape how we work, support our teams and move the business forward.

You will have room to bring ideas, improve how things are done and see the results of your work. If you enjoy connecting people, making sense of complex issues and turning decisions into action, this role offers the opportunity to do all three.

We would like to hear from you

We are building a team with a range of backgrounds and perspectives, and we value people who bring different ways of thinking and working. If this role interests you but you do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply.

H55 is committed to building an inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals regardless of nationality, gender, disability, religion, sexual orientation, or age.

About Us:

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage.

Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it.


About the role:

As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission.

This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. You'll work across our deployment and infrastructure-as-code and partner closely with product engineering to feed reliability learnings back into the platform. If you like operating serious distributed systems at scale and turning firefighting into engineered reliability, this role is for you.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds

  • Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows

  • Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes

  • Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable

  • Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go

  • Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar

You're a great fit if you:

  • Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations

  • Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud

  • Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost

  • Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents

  • Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps

  • Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code.

  • Bring sound production judgment and document your work clearly for other engineers

  • Bonus: experience operating a large-scale search or distributed data system, database operations, dedicated / enterprise-deployed software, or AI / enterprise-search infrastructure in regulated domains

What you can look forward to:

  • Owning the reliability of systems that the world's leading law firms rely on: real scale, real impact

  • Deep, hands-on work with modern infrastructure: distributed search at very large scale, container orchestration across multiple clouds, and a mature infrastructure-as-code and GitOps stack

  • A rigorous, high-urgency engineering culture founded by ex-Google search engineers and ETH Zurich AI PhDs

  • The chance to build the reliability discipline, SLOs, incident practice, automation, from a strong foundation, not inherit a rigid one

  • A collaborative team in Zurich shaping how AI transforms professional knowledge work

At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Commercially driven. You care about revenue, pipeline, and closing deals, not just having interesting scientific conversations.

  • Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.

  • Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

  • Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

  • Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

  • Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

  • Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

  • Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

  • Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

  • Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

  • Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

  • Lab automation experience is a strong plus. Familiarity with PyHamilton, PyLabRobot, Opentrons, or similar tooling helps — as does a background in robotics, industrial automation, IoT, or embedded systems.

  • Maker and hacker attitude. You like figuring out how closed systems work and building the thing that makes them work better. Bonus if you're comfortable with electronics, microcontrollers, or a 3D printer when an integration needs a physical fix.

  • AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

  • Self-starter and independent. You define what needs building from how the lab actually works, not just what's in the ticket.

  • Reliability-minded. The lab runs 24/7; you design systems where one instrument failing doesn't cascade through the whole work cell.

Biology background not required — but you should be excited that the code runs real experiments.

About the Role

You'll build out the data science layer of Adaptyv's foundry — the work that turns tens of thousands of raw, messy experimental readouts into clean, trustworthy, structured data that our customers, our models, and our own scientists can rely on. Binding (BLI/SPR), developability, biophysical, and functional assays all produce data at scale; your job is to make that data correct, comparable, and useful.

This sits at the intersection of three things: data quality (is this number real, or an artifact?), bioinformatics (linking experimental results back to sequence, structure, and protein design), and dataset building (turning foundry output into the kind of high-quality, benchmarkable data that frontier AI labs actually want). You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with the lab scientists who run the assays, the software team who own the pipelines, and the customers who train models on what we produce. This is a hands-on build role, not a management one.

What You'll Do

This is a build role, not a service role. For your first months you are making libraries, running selections, working out why a round collapsed, and turning what works into something the automation team can run without you.

What You'll Do

  • Build the libraries. Oligo pools, combinatorial assembly, barcoding. More campaigns fail here than at selection.

  • Run selections end to end, including the call on whether a round enriched real binders or just fast growers.

  • Pick the platform per campaign and stand it up. Based on the library and the target, not on what you happened to use last.

  • Own the sequencing analysis. You don't need to be a bioinformatician, but you can't be waiting on one.

  • Hand off to automation. A protocol that only works when you personally run it isn't finished.

  • Close the loop. Selected designs get expressed and measured on BLI and SPR by the team next door. That tells you whether the selection worked.

What We're Looking For

  • MSc / PhD in molecular biology, protein engineering, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years running display and selection yourself.

  • You have set up a display platform, not just used one. This is the core requirement. Built the library, got the selection working, and produced binders that held up in an independent assay. Managing outsourced CRO campaigns is not the same thing.

  • Depth in at least one display format and working literacy across the rest. We are not fixed on which one.

  • High-diversity cloning, and an understanding of where bias enters a pool and what it costs you later.

  • NGS as a routine tool, and FACS if you have it.

  • Enough Python or R to analyze your own data without joining a queue.

  • You use AI tools seriously. It's 2026 and we run on Claude Code across the company. You also need the judgment to check what comes back.

  • A self-starter. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue. You decide what to build, build it, and tell us what you learned.

About the Role

We are building the most automated lab in the world, and that does not stop at the bench. A company that AI agents can run experiments in has to automate everything around the experiment too — procurement, hiring, admin, and finance. Finance is one of the most automatable functions in any company and almost nobody has actually done it. We intend to.

That is the job: build an AI-powered finance stack. Our ledger, billing, cards and payroll all expose APIs, and we already close the books against them programmatically rather than by hand. You would take that much further, to where the model, the close, the cash view and the margin analysis largely run themselves, and your week goes on the decisions instead of the reconciliation.

You would be our first finance hire, and it is hands-on. You will build the forecast, run the close across two entities, own cash, and be the person who can say what a protein actually costs us to make.

What You'll Do

  • Own the forecast. Both directions: bottom-up from lab capacity, throughput and price per protein, and top-down P&L, burn and runway.

  • Own gross margin. What does an experiment actually cost us — DNA, reagents, consumables, instrument time, labour? Which products and which customers lose us money?

  • Own pricing, with commercial. What we charge, why, and where the floor is. Pricing at a lab company is a finance question wearing a sales hat.

  • Own the close. Group consolidation and intercompany management. Make it fast, make it correct, make it boring.

  • Own cash. Bank and card accounts across Switzerland and the US, AP runs, AR collection, payment timing. Know where the money is and where it is going before anyone asks.

  • Keep us compliant. Tax, VAT, audit, payroll, and the external firms we work with. You are not a lawyer or an accountant, but you know when to call one.

  • Investor reporting, fundraising support, and treasury management.

  • Equipment leasing and asset management. The lab runs on millions of francs of instruments. Lease or buy, how we finance it, what it does to the balance sheet, and keeping the asset register honest as we expand.

  • Automate all of the above.

What We're Looking For

  • You have built a finance function, not just worked in one. Several years in finance at a startup that actually scaled, and ideally you were early enough to have set things up rather than inherited them.

  • You can build a real model. Not a template. A model that ties operational reality — throughput, yield, capacity, headcount — to cash, and that survives someone pulling on it.

  • You write code, or you are visibly about to. SQL at minimum, Python ideally. This is the hard requirement most finance candidates will fail, and we mean it. We run on Claude Code across the company, and every system finance touches has an API behind it. The best version of this person automates their own function, writes their own tooling, and finds leverage the rest of us have not thought of. If your instinct is that finance is a spreadsheet-and-portal job, we will frustrate each other.

  • You understand the cost structure of a physical business. Reagents, instruments, consumables, capex versus COGS, yield loss. Lab, hardware, or manufacturing backgrounds all translate. Pure SaaS finance does not, on its own.

  • Swiss and European finance experience. VAT, social charges, employment law. A US entity alongside a Swiss one is a plus.

  • Ambitious, and in it for the company. We want someone who intends to be running finance at a much larger Adaptyv in three years, and who cares about what we are building rather than the title on the door.

  • Trustworthy with everything. Salaries, revenue, investor communications, board material. All of it crosses your desk.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a room with a customer, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing.

The centre of gravity is the numbers: the model, the close, cash, margin, pricing, and the board pack. That is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on. Procurement is a separate hire and the two of you will be joined at the hip on cost, but the sourcing and the vendor relationships are not yours to run.

One thing it is not: a bookkeeping seat. The mechanical layer is handled, and if that is the job you want, this one will bore you.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most first-finance-hires at a startup spend three years cleaning up a SaaS P&L. Here, the finance question and the product question are the same question: an automated lab is a machine for converting money into experimental data, and how efficiently it does that is literally the business. You will be building the model of that machine, at a company that is about to expand it several-fold, while it is being used by the best pharma companies and the best AI labs in the world. And you will do it with a founding team that will hand you the API keys and get out of your way.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

What You'll Do

  • Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

  • Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

  • Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

  • Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

  • Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

  • Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

  • Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

  • Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).

What We're Looking For

  • MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

  • Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

  • Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

  • Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

  • You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

  • A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

  • A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

  • Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it.

  • Comfortable in front of customers. Many are PhD-level scientists at pharma companies and AI labs, and they will push back. You should enjoy that conversation rather than dread it.

  • Able to explain hard things simply. Some customers are biophysicists. Some are ML researchers who have never touched a pipette. You adjust without condescending to either.

  • Honest about uncertainty. When the data is ambiguous, you say so, to us and to the customer. We would much rather flag a weak result than ship a confident wrong one.

  • Familiarity with other biophysical or functional assays (DSF, HPLC, plate-based activity assays) is a plus.
